newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria ex-premier barred from presidential poll.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria ex-premier barred from presidential poll.

text.p: Bulgarian former prime minister Reneta Indzhova on Monday said she would appeal to the Supreme Court against a refusal by the Central Electoral Committee (CEC) to register her as a presidential candidate.

The CEC barred Indzhova's candidacy on Sunday as her vice-presidential nominee, General Stoyan Tsonkov, has not been released from the army in line with electoral law but is still a serving officer, a CEC spokeswoman said.

Indzhova, Bulgaria's self-styled "Iron Lady", said she had informed President Zhelyu Zhelev that she would "oppose the politicians who did not let her participate in the presidential election", state news agency BTA quoted her as saying.
"Releasing an army officer for pursuing his candidacy for elections does not precede registration but is a result of it under the defence and army law," she told a news conference.
Indzhova was leaving for the United States later on Monday to attend an economic conference.
She said she would give there a news conference to tell "the world that Bulgaria was far from a democracy".
An opinion poll showed that the anti-communist opposition's candidate, lawyer Petar Stoyanov, is on course to win the next presidential election due on October 27.

Some 30 percent of the 1,448 people surveyed earlier this month said they intended to vote for Stoyanov, of the main opposition Union of Democratic Forces, while 24 percent said they would back the ruling Socialist Party's candidate, Culture Minister Ivan Marazov.
Other contenders, including Indzhova, a 42-year-old economist, were a long way behind the two main candidates.
Incumbent Zhelyu Zhelev, a strong critic of the current government, will not be seeking reelection.
